source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម) - "ដំណាំក្រូចពោធិសាត់" (Pursat Orange Cultivation Guide), 2016, 26pp
text:
Grafting is the method most recommended for producing quality Pursat orange planting stock. The source describes several related approaches used in nurseries: T-budding, wedge/veneer grafting, and whip-and-tongue grafting, all performed by joining a bud or shoot piece (មេក) from a proven, high-yielding, disease-free mother tree onto separate rootstock (ដើមគល់ / Root Stock).

Rootstock is usually raised from seed and grown for about 1 year in the nursery until it reaches roughly finger thickness (about 0.4 cm) at a height of around 15-20 cm above ground - this is the point where the graft union is made. Before grafting, growers check that the rootstock bark peels easily, which confirms sap is flowing well and the union is likely to take.

For T-budding, a T-shaped cut is made in the rootstock bark, a bud shield about 1 cm long is inserted from the scion wood, and the union is wrapped tightly with plastic grafting tape to exclude air and moisture. Growers check the graft after about 2 to 3 weeks: a bud that is still green and swelling indicates a successful union, while a dried, brown bud means the graft has failed and should be redone. Once the bud has clearly taken and begun to grow, the top of the rootstock above the graft union is cut away to force all growth into the new scion.
